crossCutting.issue: No REST verbs beyond GET/POST: every create/update/withdraw is a POST with an action discriminator; no PUT/PATCH/DELETE handlers exist and no server actions ("use server" not found).

DB-enforced immutability: app.reject_rewrite BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE triggers cover almost all business tables; only app.mission, mission_market, commercial_intent, meeting, follow_up, opportunity, membership, relationship, evidence_state, inbox_notification.read_at, saved_mission.removed_at and queue tables are updatable, each with guard/version triggers. No immutable business record was found to be editable or hard-deletable.

Hard DELETEs are limited to transient/credential rows: session proofs (cascading request_attestation), execution grants, identity.verification (team/network invitations), twoFactor/session on authenticator reset, mission_mail_recipient addresses, outcome_projection rebuild, identity.assurance.
Idempotency is consistent in customer modules (commandId ledgers with conflict detection) but absent in operator membership change and notification preferences.

Optimistic concurrency (expectedVersion/expectedSeq/expectedPosition) is used in nearly all revisioned customer and billing modules; exceptions: Moves set, programme attendance, operator membership change, notification preferences.

Operator workspace lists are hard-capped (LIMIT 50/100/200/1000) with no cursor for evidence, communications, meetings, network tasks and counterparty detail sections; customer module lists use keyset pagination.

app.inbox_record lets any signed-in staff or customer write an inbox item for any recipient id (only a tenant-membership check for staff when a tenant is named); reachable through server-side notify().
No archive/close lifecycle for top-level containers: customer workspace, programme and customer account have create/read only.
Money correction paths: ledger entries have reversals and invoices have credit notes, but payment observations (sample and real) have no reversal or void.
The operator workspace route returns HTTP 201 for every write action, including updates and revocations, and maps DB errors to generic 409/403 text.
